question: What is the most common histological category of ovarian cancer?
explanation: Epithelial tumors account for the vast majority of ovarian malignancies encountered in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h1)

question: Which ovarian cancer cell type typically affects younger populations and originates from egg-producing cells?
explanation: Germ cell malignancies develop from gamete-producing cells and predominantly appear in children and young adults. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h1)

question: Which genetic mutation is most strongly linked to hereditary ovarian and breast cancer syndromes?
explanation: Inherited mutations in BRCA genes disrupt DNA repair pathways, multiplying the risk of both ovarian and breast malignancies. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h2)

question: Why does nulliparity act as a risk factor for epithelial ovarian cancer?

options.A: It decreases circulating progesterone levels during adolescent development
options.B: It causes chronic inflammatory changes within the fallopian tube fimbriae
options.C: It accelerates the natural process of premature ovarian failure
options.D: It results in an uninterrupted, higher total number of lifetime ovulatory cycles

explanation: Each ovulation causes localized surface disruption and repair, which statistically increases opportunities for malignant cellular transformation over time. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h2)

question: Which symptom is most characteristic of early-stage ovarian cancer?

options.A: Massive painless hematuria accompanied by dysuria
options.B: Acute, severe lower quadrant pain radiating down the leg
options.C: Sudden high fever with purulent vaginal discharge
options.D: Vague gastrointestinal complaints and abdominal bloating

explanation: Because early symptoms mimic benign conditions like dyspepsia or irritable bowel syndrome, diagnosis is frequently delayed. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h3)

question: A forty-five-year-old woman presents to the clinic with persistent early satiety, pelvic pressure, and unexplained abdominal enlargement lasting several weeks. What condition should the nurse suspect?
explanation: The triad of persistent bloating, pelvic pressure, and early satiety in a mature adult warrants urgent investigation for ovarian pathology. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h3)

question: What is the primary serum tumor marker utilized in the evaluation of suspected epithelial ovarian cancer?
explanation: Cancer Antigen 125 is elevated in a significant proportion of epithelial ovarian carcinomas, though it is not exclusively diagnostic. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h4)

question: Why is CA-125 alone considered inadequate as a general screening tool for asymptomatic women?

options.A: It can be elevated in benign conditions such as pregnancy or pelvic inflammatory disease
options.B: It only detects tumors after they have already metastasized to the brain
options.C: It fails to register in patients carrying genetic BRCA mutations
options.D: It degrades rapidly in blood samples kept at room temperature

explanation: Lack of specificity leads to high false-positive rates, making CA-125 unsuitable for mass screening without imaging backup. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h4)

question: At which FIGO stage is ovarian cancer strictly confined to one or both ovaries without pelvic extension?
explanation: Stage I disease is localized solely to the ovarian tissue, offering the most favorable prognosis. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h5)

question: Which finding indicates that an ovarian cancer has progressed to Stage III?

options.A: Presence of malignant cells within pleural fluid effusions
options.B: Spread into the peritoneal cavity or retroperitoneal lymph nodes
options.C: Involvement limited strictly to the muscular wall of the uterus
options.D: Microscopic invasion restricted to the single layer of surface epithelium

explanation: Stage III involves extension outside the true pelvis into the peritoneal cavity or regional lymph nodes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h5)

question: Which drug classes form the standard chemotherapy backbone for treating epithelial ovarian cancer?
explanation: Combinations like carboplatin and paclitaxel are established first-line chemotherapeutic treatments following surgical debulking. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of primary cytoreductive surgery in advanced ovarian cancer?

options.A: To remove as much visible tumor bulk as physically possible to enhance chemotherapy efficacy
options.B: To eradicate microscopic disease exclusively within the central nervous system
options.C: To permanently preserve future childbearing potential in premenopausal females
options.D: To prevent the development of secondary postoperative wound infections

explanation: Maximal debulking leaves minimal residual disease, improving the effectiveness of subsequent systemic chemotherapy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h6)

question: Which major complication must nurses actively monitor for in postoperative and oncology patients with ovarian cancer?
explanation: Malignant disease processes combined with major pelvic surgery significantly heighten the risk of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h7)

question: Why is nutritional monitoring particularly challenging for individuals with advanced ovarian cancer?

options.A: Patients develop an aversion to all oral liquids immediately following surgery
options.B: Hypermetabolic states triggered by the cancer cells eliminate all dietary proteins
options.C: Chemotherapy permanently destroys the functional lining of the human esophagus
options.D: Tumor burden and ascites cause gastric compression, leading to early satiety and poor intake

explanation: Physical pressure from abdominal masses and fluid accumulation limits stomach capacity, requiring careful, frequent nutritional planning. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h7)
